name: Cook a recipe neither of you has made before
description: Pick something slightly ambitious from a cookbook or a random recipe site and cook it together, start to finish.

name: Pack a picnic and walk to the nearest park
description: Nothing fancy — bread, cheese, fruit, a blanket. The point is sitting outside with no screens.

name: Go for a sunrise walk
description: Set an alarm, grab coffee in a flask, and watch the sky change together before the day starts properly.

name: Board game tournament for two
description: Pick two or three games and play a best-of-three series. Loser makes tea.

name: Bike somewhere you've never been
description: Pick a direction neither of you usually goes and follow it for twenty minutes, then turn around.

name: Visit a museum or gallery
description: Doesn't have to be the big famous one — a small local gallery works just as well.

name: Start a jigsaw puzzle
description: Put something on in the background and work on it together over an evening or two.

name: Find somewhere to swim outdoors
description: A lido, a lake, the sea — whatever's nearby and open.

name: Build a home cinema night
description: Blackout the room, make proper snacks, pick a film you've both been meaning to watch.

name: Wander a farmers market or car boot sale
description: No shopping list. Just browse, taste samples, and see what you end up with.

name: Half-day hike
description: Pick a trail you haven't done, pack proper snacks and water, and commit to the whole thing.

name: Try making a cocktail you've never had
description: Look up a recipe, buy whatever's missing, and make a mess of the kitchen together.

name: Photo walk, phones only
description: Set a loose theme (doors, textures, dogs) and each take ten photos while you walk.

name: Cafe crawl
description: Pick two or three coffee shops you've never been to and have a small something at each.

name: Stargazing somewhere dark
description: Drive or walk out past the streetlights, bring a blanket, and just look up for a while.

name: Learn a short dance together
description: Find a beginner tutorial online and actually follow it through, even badly.

name: Book a one-off craft class
description: Pottery, life drawing, candle-making — whatever's running locally this week.

name: Scenic drive with no destination
description: Pick a direction, put on a playlist, and stop wherever looks interesting.

name: Cook a big meal and invite someone over
description: More work, more reward — plan a menu and host, even if it's casual.

name: Run together, whatever pace
description: Doesn't need to be fast or far — the point is doing it side by side.

name: Card game marathon
description: Pick a two-player card game and play until one of you hits a target score.

name: Browse a bookshop, then read on a bench
description: Each pick something for the other, then sit outside and read the first chapter.

name: Eat a cuisine you've never tried
description: Find a restaurant for food neither of you has eaten before and go in with no expectations.

name: Try an indoor climbing wall
description: Most centres do taster sessions — no experience needed, just shoes you can borrow.

name: Start a small garden or balcony project
description: A few pots, some herbs or flowers, an afternoon getting your hands dirty.

name: Karaoke at home
description: Find a karaoke playlist online and take turns picking songs. No judgment.

name: Do a free walking tour of your own city
description: Look up a self-guided or free tour of somewhere near you you've never actually explored properly.

name: Bake something from scratch
description: Bread, a cake, anything with a few fiddly steps you have to do together.

name: Plan a do-nothing afternoon
description: No activity at all — just the same room, same blanket, no agenda.

name: Mini golf or an arcade
description: Pure low-stakes competition. Loser buys the next round of something.

name: Swim at Brockwell Lido
description: A 50m outdoor pool framed by Grade II-listed art deco buildings, open year-round. Book a swim session ahead through Active Lambeth.

name: Wander the walled garden in Brockwell Park
description: An Old English flower garden with roses, exotic plants and ornamental ponds, a five-minute walk from Herne Hill station.

name: Visit the Brockwell Park Community Greenhouses
description: A volunteer-run walled garden, orchard and pair of greenhouses sharing a wall with the Walled Garden. Open Thursday to Sunday.

name: Browse Herne Hill Market
description: A Sunday market along Railton Road right by the station, with 50+ stalls of local produce, crafts and street food.

name: Track taster session at Herne Hill Velodrome
description: A cycling track used in the 1948 Olympics, right next to Brockwell Park. Adult taster sessions run Saturday afternoons — book ahead.

name: Visit Dulwich Picture Gallery
description: England's first public art gallery, known for its Old Masters and striking Soane-designed building. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am-5pm.

name: Hire a boat on Dulwich Park's lake
description: A boating lake plus a big network of paths and hidden ponds to walk, with a cafe for afterwards and usually a lot of dogs.

name: Follow the Dulwich Street Art Walk
description: A self-guided trail of murals around Dulwich Village, including the mosaic-covered House of Dreams.

name: Explore the Horniman Museum
description: Free galleries covering anthropology, natural history and musical instruments, plus an aquarium and a butterfly house, in Forest Hill.

name: Picnic in the Horniman's gardens
description: Sixteen acres with some of the best skyline views in south London, a bandstand and a small animal enclosure. Free to enter.

name: Walk the dinosaur trail at Crystal Palace Park
description: Recently restored Victorian concrete dinosaur sculptures scattered around the park's lake — free to visit any time.

name: Get lost in the Crystal Palace Park maze
description: A 160-foot hedge maze, with a skatepark and local history museum nearby if you want to make a day of it.

name: Crystal Palace Flea vintage market
description: A vintage market in the park's Bowl area with 30+ traders selling homeware, designer clothing and retro furniture.

name: West Norwood Feast street food market
description: Over 100 stalls across four sites on the first Sunday of the month (April-December) — food, drink and crafts.

name: Wander West Norwood Cemetery
description: One of London's 'Magnificent Seven' Victorian cemeteries, with grand tombs and quiet, overgrown paths — an odd, peaceful walk.

name: Food crawl through Brixton Village and Market Row
description: Covered arcades packed with independent restaurants, bars and shops — pick two or three small plates each and compare notes.

name: Catch a film at the Ritzy
description: One of London's oldest picture houses, open since 1911, showing independent and mainstream films on Brixton Oval.

name: Street food and live music at Hootananny
description: A Victorian pub in Brixton with a garden of street-food stalls (jerk chicken, Mexican, wood-fired pizza) and regular live music nights.

name: Rooftop Cinema Club at the Bussey Building
description: Summer al fresco film screenings on the Bussey Building roof in Peckham, with food and drink delivered to your seat.

name: Cocktails at the Bussey rooftop bar
description: A multilevel bar with 360-degree views over Peckham, plus pizza — good for a date-night drink with a view.

name: Ice skating at Streatham Ice and Leisure
description: One of London's only permanent Olympic-sized rinks, with public skating sessions through the week.

name: Walk Streatham Common and the Rookery
description: Open lawns and a paddling pool on the Common, with a walled Edwardian garden and waterfall tucked into the Rookery at the top.

name: Explore Peckham Levels
description: A former multi-storey car park turned food hall, studios and bars across several floors — an easy wander with food at the end.

name: Walk Sydenham Hill Wood
description: The largest remaining fragment of the old Great North Wood, with a Victorian ruin folly hidden among the trees near the Horniman.

name: Browse Electric Avenue market
description: Brixton's historic market street for bargains, fabric, fruit and veg, and street food stalls.

name: Explore Dacres Wood Nature Reserve
description: A small, little-known nature reserve tucked near the Horniman — good for a quiet detour after the museum.

name: Smithfield Market at dawn
description: An 800-year-old meat market near Farringdon — early stallholders pack up around 7am, so go early for the atmosphere.

name: Catch a show at the Barbican Centre
description: Theatre, classical concerts and film screenings near Farringdon, plus a conservatory with 1,500+ tropical plants.

name: Browse Leather Lane Market
description: A lively street market for food, coffee and handmade goods just by Farringdon station.

name: Find the memorial wall at Postman's Park
description: A small City park with a covered wall of 54 Victorian plaques honouring ordinary people who died saving others — a quiet, odd detour near Farringdon.

name: Walk the Millennium Bridge
description: The 'Wobbly Bridge' between St Paul's and Tate Modern, with one of London's best skyline views from the middle.

name: Explore Tate Modern
description: Free entry, a vast Turbine Hall for rotating installations, and a top-floor terrace view over the Thames — a short walk from Blackfriars.

name: Climb to St Paul's Golden Gallery
description: 528 steps up for a sweeping view across the Thames, the Shard and beyond — book ahead.

name: Shop and eat at Coal Drops Yard
description: A converted Victorian coal depot turned shopping and dining destination next to Granary Square, King's Cross.

name: Walk the canal from Granary Square
description: Start at Granary Square's fountains and follow the Regent's Canal towpath toward Camden, Primrose Hill or Little Venice.

name: Catch an immersive show at Lightroom
description: A four-storey digital art space on Lewis Cubitt Square, King's Cross, with large-scale immersive shows that change periodically — check what's currently on.

name: See a free exhibition at the British Library
description: Treasures like the Magna Carta and Beatles lyrics sit in the free permanent gallery, steps from St Pancras.

name: Tour Camden Town Brewery
description: Tours and tastings near Kentish Town West — good for a Saturday afternoon detour.

name: Visit Kentish Town City Farm
description: A small city farm in the middle of Kentish Town, with animals, a cafe and a genuinely surprising amount of quiet.

name: Walk up Parliament Hill, Hampstead Heath
description: A steep walk from Kentish Town up through the Heath for one of London's best skyline views, best at sunset.

name: Visit the Freud Museum
description: Sigmund Freud's final home in West Hampstead, preserved much as he left it, including the original psychoanalysis couch.

name: West Hampstead farmers' market
description: A Saturday market right outside West Hampstead Thameslink station — good for breakfast before a wander down West End Lane.

name: Explore Verulamium Park and Roman ruins
description: Roman walls, mosaics and Britain's only visible Roman theatre, set in parkland a 20-minute direct train from Herne Hill.

name: Visit St Albans Cathedral
description: Free entry, 13th-century wall paintings and England's only surviving medieval town belfry clock tower next door.

name: Browse St Albans market
description: A large outdoor market through the historic city centre, named Britain's best large outdoor market in 2024.

name: Pint at Ye Olde Fighting Cocks
description: Reputedly one of England's oldest pubs, tucked by the river in St Albans — a good end to a day trip.
